context.body: When David was a little past the top, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with a couple of donkeys saddled, and on them two hundred loaves of bread,….
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Ziba brings supplies and accuses Mephibosheth; David grants property, then Shimei curses and throws stones while David refuses Abishai’s proposal to kill him.
observations.label: Provision, accusation, and cursing meet David on the road: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, Ziba, Mephibosheth, Shimei, Abishai, servants, and warriors, Bahurim and the wilderness road, bringing provisions, accusing, granting land, cursing, throwing stones, proposing death, refusing, and enduring visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: Provision, accusation, and cursing meet David on the road: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: David, Ziba, Mephibosheth, Shimei, Abishai, servants, and warriors · Bahurim and the wilderness road · bringing provisions, accusing, granting land, cursing, throwing stones, proposing death, refusing, and enduring · David makes one quick property judgment and leaves another hostile act to possible divine regard
observations.label: Relationships named in 2 Samuel 16:1–14

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 16:1–14 as its own exile, return, and rebellion David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places David makes one quick property judgment and leaves another hostile act to possible divine regard inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
